result:
12 of the 150 rules didn't match their docstrings. I fixed the code for all of them and left the docstrings unchanged. I ran a script that rebuilds each rule from its docstring and the module's common rules and compares every rule over a wide range of qty and unit values. Before the fix it found exactly these 12 mismatches. After the fix all 150 rules match.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 28, 44, 59 | Marked "whole" in the docstring, but the discount only applied to units above the threshold, `(qty - threshold) * unit` | Discount now applies to the whole order, `base * pct // 100` |
| 49, 101, 115 | Used `qty > N`, so ordering exactly the threshold quantity got no discount | Changed to `qty >= N` |
| 63 | The cap only kicked in once the discount passed 20,000 won, so discounts between 10,000 and 20,000 weren't capped | Always caps at 10,000 |
| 77 | The cap only kicked in once the discount passed 100,000 won | Always caps at 50,000 |
| 79, 144 | Capped the price before calculating the discount, instead of capping the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it (30,000 / 10,000) |
| 130 | Capped the price above the threshold, `(qty-10)*unit`, before calculating the discount | Calculate the marginal discount first, then cap it at 10,000 |
| 150 | Used `round(...)`, so discounts could round up | Changed to floor division `// 100` |

A few rules are written differently from the rest but behave correctly, so I left them alone: 11, 14, 88, 111, 118, 119, 142, 53, 80, 126, 35 and 64. Their conditions use forms like `5 <= qty` or `not qty < 10`, some write the base as `(qty * unit)`, and some cap with an `if` instead of `min`. There were no tests in the folder, so the docstring comparison script was the only check. I also confirmed that `quote` and the negative-input `ValueError` still work.

STATUS: DONE
